\chapter{Boolean Analysis --- Norms}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomVariables.Norms
\section{Overview}
Subtracting an independent centered copy increases every affine norm of exponent at least one. An independent uniform sign also dominates the corresponding affine norm with the original variable halved, including the essential-supremum endpoint.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Symmetrization increases affine norms]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.symmetrization_norm_le}
\leanok
\difficulty{6}
Let $X,X^{\prime}$ be independent identically distributed real random variables on a probability space, let $1\le q\le\infty$, assume $X\in L^q$ and $\E X=0$, and let $a\in\bbr$. Then $\|a+X\|_q\le\|a+X-X^{\prime}\|_q$, with the essential supremum at $q=\infty$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Random-sign comparison]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.randomization_norm_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsRademacherRV, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsRademacherRV.map_eq}
\difficulty{6}
Let $X$ be a centered real random variable on a probability space, let $1\le q\le\infty$, and assume $X\in L^q$. If $r$ is an independent measurable uniform sign in $\{-1,1\}$, then for every $a\in\bbr$, $\|a+X/2\|_q\le\|a+rX\|_q$, including the essential-supremum norm.
\end{theorem}
